Payalatawas therefore said to him, “Are you a king then?” Yashawai answered, “You say that I am a king. For this reason I have been born, and for this reason I have come into the world, that I should testify to the truth. Everyone who is of the truth listens to my voice.”
Payalatawas said to him, “What is truth?” When he had said this, he went out again to the Jews, and said to them, “I find no basis for a charge against him.
But you have a custom, that I should release someone to you at the Passover. Therefore, do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?”
Then they all shouted again, saying, “Not this man, but Barabbas!” Now Barabbas was a robber.
So Payalatawas then took Yashawai, and flogged him.
The soldiers twisted thorns into a crown, and put it on his head, and dressed him in a purple garment.
They kept saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!” and they kept slapping him.
Then Payalatawas went out again, and said to them, “Behold, I bring him out to you, that you may know that I find no basis for a charge against him.”
Yashawai therefore came out, wearing the crown of thorns and the purple garment. Payalatawas said to them, “Behold, the man!”

When therefore the chief priests and the officers saw him, they shouted, saying, “Crucify! Crucify!” Payalatawas said to them, “Take him yourselves, and crucify him, for I find no basis for a charge against him.”
The Jews answered him, “We have a law, and by our law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of Alahayam.”
When therefore Payalatawas heard this saying, he was more afraid.
He entered into the Praetorium again, and said to Yashawai, “Where are you from?” But Yashawai gave him no answer.
Payalatawas therefore said to him, “Aren’t you speaking to me? Don’t you know that I have power to release you and have power to crucify you?”
Yashawai answered, “You would have no power at all against me, unless it were given to you from above. Therefore he who delivered me to you has greater sin.”
At this, Payalatawas was seeking to release him, but the Jews cried out, saying, “If you release this man, you aren’t Qayasar’s friend! Everyone who makes himself a king speaks against Qayasar!”
When Payalatawas therefore heard these words, he brought Yashawai out and sat down on the judgment seat at a place called “The Pavement”, but in Hebrew, “Gabbatha.”
Now it was the Preparation Day of the Passover, at about the sixth hour. He said to the Jews, “Behold, your King!”
They cried out, “Away with him! Away with him! Crucify him!” Payalatawas said to them, “Shall I crucify your King?” The chief priests answered, “We have no king but Qayasar!”
So then he delivered him to them to be crucified. So they took Yashawai and led him away.
He went out, bearing his cross, to the place called “The Place of a Skull”, which is called in Hebrew, “Golgotha”,
where they crucified him, and with him two others, on either side one, and Yashawai in the middle.
Payalatawas wrote a title also, and put it on the cross. There was written, “JESUS OF NAZARETH, THE KING OF THE JEWS.”
Therefore many of the Jews read this title, for the place where Yashawai was crucified was near the city; and it was written in Hebrew, in Latin, and in Greek.
The chief priests of the Jews therefore said to Payalatawas, “Don’t write, ‘The King of the Jews,’ but, ‘he said, “I am King of the Jews.” ’ ”
Payalatawas answered, “What I have written, I have written.”
Then the soldiers, when they had crucified Yashawai, took his garments and made four parts, to every soldier a part; and also the coat. Now the coat was without seam, woven from the top throughout.

Then they said to one another, “Let’s not tear it, but cast lots for it to decide whose it will be,” that the Scripture might be fulfilled, which says, “They parted my garments among them. For my cloak they cast lots.” Therefore the soldiers did these things.
But standing by Yashawai’ cross were his mother, his mother’s sister, Marayam the wife of Clopas, and Marayam Magdalene.
Therefore when Yashawai saw his mother, and the disciple whom he loved standing there, he said to his mother, “Woman, behold, your son!”
Then he said to the disciple, “Behold, your mother!” From that hour, the disciple took her to his own home.
After this, Yashawai, seeing that all things were now finished, that the Scripture might be fulfilled, said, “I am thirsty.”
Now a vessel full of vinegar was set there; so they put a sponge full of the vinegar on hyssop, and held it at his mouth.
When Yashawai therefore had received the vinegar, he said, “It is finished.” He bowed his head, and gave up his spirit.

Therefore the Jews, because it was the Preparation Day, so that the bodies wouldn’t remain on the cross on the Sabbath (for that Sabbath was a special one), asked of Payalatawas that their legs might be broken, and that they might be taken away.
Therefore the soldiers came, and broke the legs of the first, and of the other who was crucified with him;
but when they came to Yashawai, and saw that he was already dead, they didn’t break his legs.
However one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out.
He who has seen has testified, and his testimony is true. He knows that he tells the truth, that you may believe.
For these things happened that the Scripture might be fulfilled, “A bone of him will not be broken.”
Again another Scripture says, “They will look on him whom they pierced.”

After these things, Yawasap of Arimathaea, being a disciple of Yashawai, but secretly for fear of the Jews, asked of Payalatawas that he might take away Yashawai’ body. Payalatawas gave him permission. He came therefore and took away his body.
Nicodemus, who at first came to Yashawai by night, also came bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred Roman pounds.
So they took Yashawai’ body, and bound it in linen cloths with the spices, as the custom of the Jews is to bury.
Now in the place where he was crucified there was a garden. In the garden was a new tomb in which no man had ever yet been laid.
Then because of the Jews’ Preparation Day (for the tomb was near at hand) they laid Yashawai there.
Now on the first day of the week, Marayam Magdalene went early, while it was still dark, to the tomb, and saw the stone taken away from the tomb.

Therefore she ran and came to Shamaiwan Kayapaa and to the other disciple whom Yashawai loved, and said to them, “They have taken away the Adanay out of the tomb, and we don’t know where they have laid him!”
Therefore Kayapaa and the other disciple went out, and they went toward the tomb.
They both ran together. The other disciple outran Kayapaa, and came to the tomb first.
Stooping and looking in, he saw the linen cloths lying, yet he didn’t enter in.
Then Shamaiwan Kayapaa came, following him, and entered into the tomb. He saw the linen cloths lying,
and the cloth that had been on his head, not lying with the linen cloths, but rolled up in a place by itself.
So then the other disciple who came first to the tomb also entered in, and he saw and believed.
For as yet they didn’t know the Scripture, that he must rise from the dead.
So the disciples went away again to their own homes.
But Marayam was standing outside at the tomb weeping. So as she wept, she stooped and looked into the tomb,
and she saw two angels in white sitting, one at the head, and one at the feet, where the body of Yashawai had lain.
They asked her, “Woman, why are you weeping?” She said to them, “Because they have taken away my Adanay, and I don’t know where they have laid him.”
When she had said this, she turned around and saw Yashawai standing, and didn’t know that it was Yashawai.

Yashawai said to her, “Woman, why are you weeping? Who are you looking for?” She, supposing him to be the gardener, said to him, “Sir, if you have carried him away, tell me where you have laid him, and I will take him away.”
Yashawai said to her, “Marayam.” She turned and said to him, “Rabboni!” which is to say, “Teacher!”
Yashawai said to her, “Don’t hold me, for I haven’t yet ascended to my Father; but go to my brothers and tell them, ‘I am ascending to my Father and your Father, to my Alahayam and your Alahayam.’ ”
Marayam Magdalene came and told the disciples that she had seen the Adanay, and that he had said these things to her.

When therefore it was evening on that day, the first day of the week, and when the doors were locked where the disciples were assembled, for fear of the Jews, Yashawai came and stood in the middle, and said to them, “Peace be to you.”
When he had said this, he showed them his hands and his side. The disciples therefore were glad when they saw the Adanay.
Yashawai therefore said to them again, “Peace be to you. As the Father has sent me, even so I send you.”
When he had said this, he breathed on them, and said to them, “Receive the Holy Spirit!
If you forgive anyone’s sins, they have been forgiven them. If you retain anyone’s sins, they have been retained.”
But Thaawam, one of the twelve, called Didymus, wasn’t with them when Yashawai came.

The other disciples therefore said to him, “We have seen the Adanay!” But he said to them, “Unless I see in his hands the print of the nails, put my finger into the print of the nails, and put my hand into his side, I will not believe.”
After eight days again his disciples were inside and Thaawam was with them. Yashawai came, the doors being locked, and stood in the middle, and said, “Peace be to you.”
Then he said to Thaawam, “Reach here your finger, and see my hands. Reach here your hand, and put it into my side. Don’t be unbelieving, but believing.”
Thaawam answered him, “My Adanay and my Alahayam!”
Yashawai said to him, “Because you have seen me, you have believed. Blessed are those who have not seen, and have believed.”
Therefore Yashawai did many other signs in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book;
but these are written, that you may believe that Yashawai is the Mashayach, the Son of Alahayam, and that believing you may have life in his name.
After these things, Yashawai revealed himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias. He revealed himself this way.
Shamaiwan Kayapaa, Thaawam called Didymus, Nathanaal of Cana in Galayal, and the sons of Zebedee, and two others of his disciples were together.
Shamaiwan Kayapaa said to them, “I’m going fishing.” They told him, “We are also coming with you.” They immediately went out, and entered into the boat. That night, they caught nothing.
But when day had already come, Yashawai stood on the beach, yet the disciples didn’t know that it was Yashawai.
Yashawai therefore said to them, “Children, have you anything to eat?” They answered him, “No.”
He said to them, “Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some.” They cast it therefore, and now they weren’t able to draw it in for the multitude of fish.

That disciple therefore whom Yashawai loved said to Kayapaa, “It’s the Adanay!” So when Shamaiwan Kayapaa heard that it was the Adanay, he wrapped his coat around himself (for he was naked), and threw himself into the sea.
But the other disciples came in the little boat (for they were not far from the land, but about two hundred cubits away), dragging the net full of fish.
So when they got out on the land, they saw a fire of coals there, with fish and bread laid on it.
Yashawai said to them, “Bring some of the fish which you have just caught.”
Shamaiwan Kayapaa went up, and drew the net to land, full of one hundred fifty-three great fish. Even though there were so many, the net wasn’t torn.
Yashawai said to them, “Come and eat breakfast!” None of the disciples dared inquire of him, “Who are you?” knowing that it was the Adanay.
Then Yashawai came and took the bread, gave it to them, and the fish likewise.
This is now the third time that Yashawai was revealed to his disciples after he had risen from the dead.

So when they had eaten their breakfast, Yashawai said to Shamaiwan Kayapaa, “Shamaiwan, son of Yawanah, do you love me more than these?” He said to him, “Yes, Adanay; you know that I have affection for you.” He said to him, “Feed my lambs.”
He said to him again a second time, “Shamaiwan, son of Yawanah, do you love me?” He said to him, “Yes, Adanay; you know that I have affection for you.” He said to him, “Tend my sheep.”

He said to him the third time, “Shamaiwan, son of Yawanah, do you have affection for me?” Kayapaa was grieved because he asked him the third time, “Do you have affection for me?” He said to him, “Adanay, you know everything. You know that I have affection for you.” Yashawai said to him, “Feed my sheep.

Most certainly I tell you, when you were young, you dressed yourself and walked where you wanted to. But when you are old, you will stretch out your hands, and another will dress you and carry you where you don’t want to go.”
Now he said this, signifying by what kind of death he would glorify Alahayam. When he had said this, he said to him, “Follow me.”

Then Kayapaa, turning around, saw a disciple following. This was the disciple whom Yashawai loved, the one who had also leaned on Yashawai’ breast at the supper and asked, “Adanay, who is going to betray you?”
Kayapaa seeing him, said to Yashawai, “Adanay, what about this man?”
Yashawai said to him, “If I desire that he stay until I come, what is that to you? You follow me.”

This saying therefore went out among the brothers, that this disciple wouldn’t die. Yet Yashawai didn’t say to him that he wouldn’t die, but, “If I desire that he stay until I come, what is that to you?”
This is the disciple who testifies about these things, and wrote these things. We know that his witness is true.
There are also many other things which Yashawai did, which if they would all be written, I suppose that even the world itself wouldn’t have room for the books that would be written.
The first book I wrote, Theophilus, concerned all that Yashawai began both to do and to teach,
until the day in which he was received up, after he had given commandment through the Holy Spirit to the apostles whom he had chosen.
To these he also showed himself alive after he suffered, by many proofs, appearing to them over a period of forty days, and speaking about Alahayam’s Kingdom.
Being assembled together with them, he commanded them, “Don’t depart from Yarawashalam, but wait for the promise of the Father, which you heard from me.
For Yawachanan indeed baptized in water, but you will be baptized in the Holy Spirit not many days from now.”
Therefore when they had come together, they asked him, “Adanay, are you now restoring the kingdom to Yasharaal?”
He said to them, “It isn’t for you to know times or seasons which the Father has set within his own authority.
But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you. You will be witnesses to me in Yarawashalam, in all Yahawadah and Shamarawan, and to the uttermost parts of the earth.”
When he had said these things, as they were looking, he was taken up, and a cloud received him out of their sight.
While they were looking steadfastly into the sky as he went, behold, two men stood by them in white clothing,
who also said, “You men of Galayal, why do you stand looking into the sky? This Yashawai, who was received up from you into the sky, will come back in the same way as you saw him going into the sky.”
Then they returned to Yarawashalam from the mountain called Olivet, which is near Yarawashalam, a Sabbath day’s journey away.

When they had come in, they went up into the upper room where they were staying; that is Kayapaa, Yawachanan, Yaiqab, Anadaray, Payalayapawas, Thaawam, Barathalam, Mathathayahaw, Yaiqab the son of Alphaeus, Shamaiwan the Zealot, and Yahawadah the son of Yaiqab.
All these with one accord continued steadfastly in prayer and supplication, along with the women, and Marayam the mother of Yashawai, and with his brothers.
In these days, Kayapaa stood up in the middle of the disciples (and the number of names was about one hundred twenty), and said,
“Brothers, it was necessary that this Scripture should be fulfilled, which the Holy Spirit spoke before by the mouth of Dawad concerning Yahawadah, who was guide to those who took Yashawai.
For he was counted with us, and received his portion in this ministry.
Now this man obtained a field with the reward for his wickedness, and falling headlong, his body burst open, and all his intestines gushed out.
It became known to everyone who lived in Yarawashalam that in their language that field was called ‘Akeldama,’ that is, ‘The field of blood.’
For it is written in the book of Psalms, ‘Let his habitation be made desolate. Let no one dwell in it;’ and, ‘Let another take his office.’
“Of the men therefore who have accompanied us all the time that the Adanay Yashawai went in and out among us,
beginning from the baptism of Yawachanan, to the day that he was received up from us, of these one must become a witness with us of his resurrection.”
They put forward two, Yawasap called Barsabbas, who was also called Justus, and Matthias.
They prayed and said, “You, Adanay, who know the hearts of all men, show which one of these two you have chosen
to take part in this ministry and apostleship from which Yahawadah fell away, that he might go to his own place.”
They drew lots for them, and the lot fell on Matthias, and he was counted with the eleven apostles.
Now when the day of Pentecost had come, they were all with one accord in one place.
Suddenly there came from the sky a sound like the rushing of a mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting.
Tongues like fire appeared and were distributed to them, and one sat on each of them.
They were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and began to speak with other languages, as the Spirit gave them the ability to speak.
Now there were dwelling in Yarawashalam Jews, devout men, from every nation under the sky.
When this sound was heard, the multitude came together and were bewildered, because everyone heard them speaking in his own language.
They were all amazed and marveled, saying to one another, “Behold, aren’t all these who speak Galilaeans?
How do we hear, everyone in our own native language?
Parthians, Maday, Elamites, and people from Aram, Yahawadah, Cappadocia, Pontus, Asia,
Phrygia, Pamphylia, Matzarayam, the parts of Libya around Cyrene, visitors from Rome, both Jews and proselytes,
Cretans and Arabians: we hear them speaking in our languages the mighty works of Alahayam!”
They were all amazed, and were perplexed, saying to one another, “What does this mean?”
Others, mocking, said, “They are filled with new wine.”
But Kayapaa, standing up with the eleven, lifted up his voice, and spoke out to them, “You men of Yahawadah, and all you who dwell at Yarawashalam, let this be known to you, and listen to my words.
For these aren’t drunken, as you suppose, seeing it is only the third hour of the day.
But this is what has been spoken through the prophet Yawaal:
‘It will be in the last days, says Alahayam, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh. Your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your young men will see visions. Your old men will dream dreams.
Yes, and on my servants and on my handmaidens in those days, I will pour out my Spirit, and they will prophesy.
I will show wonders in the sky above, and signs on the earth beneath: blood, and fire, and billows of smoke.
The sun will be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and glorious day of the Adanay comes.
It will be that whoever will call on the name of the Adanay will be saved.’
“Men of Yasharaal, hear these words! Yashawai of Natzarath, a man approved by Alahayam to you by mighty works and wonders and signs which Alahayam did by him among you, even as you yourselves know,
him, being delivered up by the determined counsel and foreknowledge of Alahayam, you have taken by the hand of lawless men, crucified and killed;
whom Alahayam raised up, having freed him from the agony of death, because it was not possible that he should be held by it.
For Dawad says concerning him, ‘I saw the Adanay always before my face, for he is on my right hand, that I should not be moved.
Therefore my heart was glad, and my tongue rejoiced. Moreover my flesh also will dwell in hope;
because you will not leave my soul in Hades, neither will you allow your Holy One to see decay.
You made known to me the ways of life. You will make me full of gladness with your presence.’
“Brothers, I may tell you freely of the patriarch Dawad, that he both died and was buried, and his tomb is with us to this day.
Therefore, being a prophet, and knowing that Alahayam had sworn with an oath to him that of the fruit of his body, according to the flesh, he would raise up the Mashayach to sit on his throne,
he foreseeing this spoke about the resurrection of the Mashayach, that his soul wasn’t left in Hades, and his flesh didn’t see decay.
This Yashawai Alahayam raised up, to which we all are witnesses.
Being therefore exalted by the right hand of Alahayam, and having received from the Father the promise of the Holy Spirit, he has poured out this, which you now see and hear.
For Dawad didn’t ascend into the heavens, but he says himself, ‘The Adanay said to my Adanay, “Sit by my right hand
until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.” ’
“Let all the house of Yasharaal therefore know certainly that Alahayam has made him both Adanay and Mashayach, this Yashawai whom you crucified.”
Now when they heard this, they were cut to the heart, and said to Kayapaa and the rest of the apostles, “Brothers, what shall we do?”
Kayapaa said to them, “Repent, and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Yashawai Mashayach for the forgiveness of sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
For the promise is to you, and to your children, and to all who are far off, even as many as the Adanay our Alahayam will call to himself.”
With many other words he testified, and exhorted them, saying, “Save yourselves from this crooked generation!”
Then those who gladly received his word were baptized. There were added that day about three thousand souls.
They continued steadfastly in the apostles’ teaching and fellowship, in the breaking of bread, and prayer.
Fear came on every soul, and many wonders and signs were done through the apostles.
All who believed were together, and had all things in common.
They sold their possessions and goods, and distributed them to all, according as anyone had need.
Day by day, continuing steadfastly with one accord in the temple, and breaking bread at home, they took their food with gladness and singleness of heart,
praising Alahayam, and having favor with all the people. The Adanay added to the assembly day by day those who were being saved.
Kayapaa and Yawachanan were going up into the temple at the hour of prayer, the ninth hour.

A certain man who was lame from his mother’s womb was being carried, whom they laid daily at the door of the temple which is called Beautiful, to ask gifts for the needy of those who entered into the temple.
Seeing Kayapaa and Yawachanan about to go into the temple, he asked to receive gifts for the needy.
Kayapaa, fastening his eyes on him, with Yawachanan, said, “Look at us.”
He listened to them, expecting to receive something from them.
But Kayapaa said, “I have no silver or gold, but what I have, that I give you. In the name of Yashawai Mashayach of Natzarath, get up and walk!”
He took him by the right hand and raised him up. Immediately his feet and his ankle bones received strength.
Leaping up, he stood and began to walk. He entered with them into the temple, walking, leaping, and praising Alahayam.
All the people saw him walking and praising Alahayam.
They recognized him, that it was he who used to sit begging for gifts for the needy at the Beautiful Gate of the temple. They were filled with wonder and amazement at what had happened to him.
As the lame man who was healed held on to Kayapaa and Yawachanan, all the people ran together to them in the porch that is called Shalamah’s, greatly wondering.
When Kayapaa saw it, he responded to the people, “You men of Yasharaal, why do you marvel at this man? Why do you fasten your eyes on us, as though by our own power or godliness we had made him walk?

The Alahayam of Abaraham, Yatzachaq, and Yaiqab, the Alahayam of our fathers, has glorified his Servant Yashawai, whom you delivered up, and denied in the presence of Payalatawas, when he had determined to release him.
But you denied the Holy and Righteous One and asked for a murderer to be granted to you,
and killed the Prince of life, whom Alahayam raised from the dead, to which we are witnesses.
By faith in his name, his name has made this man strong, whom you see and know. Yes, the faith which is through him has given him this perfect soundness in the presence of you all.
“Now, brothers, I know that you did this in ignorance, as did also your rulers.
But the things which Alahayam announced by the mouth of all his prophets, that Mashayach should suffer, he thus fulfilled.
“Repent therefore, and turn again, that your sins may be blotted out, so that there may come times of refreshing from the presence of the Adanay,
and that he may send Mashayach Yashawai, who was ordained for you before,
whom heaven must receive until the times of restoration of all things, which Alahayam spoke long ago by the mouth of his holy prophets.
For Mashah indeed said to the fathers, ‘The Adanay Alahayam will raise up a prophet for you from among your brothers, like me. You shall listen to him in all things whatever he says to you.
It will be that every soul that will not listen to that prophet will be utterly destroyed from among the people.’
Yes, and all the prophets from Shamawaal and those who followed after, as many as have spoken, they also told of these days.
You are the children of the prophets, and of the covenant which Alahayam made with our fathers, saying to Abaraham, ‘All the families of the earth will be blessed through your offspring.’
Alahayam, having raised up his servant Yashawai, sent him to you first to bless you, in turning away every one of you from your wickedness.”
As they spoke to the people, the priests and the captain of the temple and the Sadducees came to them,
being upset because they taught the people and proclaimed in Yashawai the resurrection from the dead.
They laid hands on them, and put them in custody until the next day, for it was now evening.
But many of those who heard the word believed, and the number of the men came to be about five thousand.
In the morning, their rulers, elders, and scribes were gathered together in Yarawashalam.
Annas the high priest was there, with Caiaphas, Yawachanan, Alexander, and as many as were relatives of the high priest.
When they had stood Kayapaa and Yawachanan in the middle of them, they inquired, “By what power, or in what name, have you done this?”
Then Kayapaa, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them, “You rulers of the people, and elders of Yasharaal,
if we are examined today concerning a good deed done to a crippled man, by what means this man has been healed,

may it be known to you all, and to all the people of Yasharaal, that in the name of Yashawai Mashayach of Natzarath, whom you crucified, whom Alahayam raised from the dead, this man stands here before you whole in him.
He is ‘the stone which was regarded as worthless by you, the builders, which has become the head of the corner.’
There is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven that is given among men, by which we must be saved!”
Now when they saw the boldness of Kayapaa and Yawachanan, and had perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they marveled. They recognized that they had been with Yashawai.
Seeing the man who was healed standing with them, they could say nothing against it.
But when they had commanded them to go aside out of the council, they conferred among themselves,
saying, “What shall we do to these men? Because indeed a notable miracle has been done through them, as can be plainly seen by all who dwell in Yarawashalam, and we can’t deny it.
But so that this spreads no further among the people, let’s threaten them, that from now on they don’t speak to anyone in this name.”
They called them, and commanded them not to speak at all nor teach in the name of Yashawai.
But Kayapaa and Yawachanan answered them, “Whether it is right in the sight of Alahayam to listen to you rather than to Alahayam, judge for yourselves,
for we can’t help telling the things which we saw and heard.”
When they had further threatened them, they let them go, finding no way to punish them, because of the people; for everyone glorified Alahayam for that which was done.
For the man on whom this miracle of healing was performed was more than forty years old.
Being let go, they came to their own company and reported all that the chief priests and the elders had said to them.
When they heard it, they lifted up their voice to Alahayam with one accord, and said, “O Adanay, you are Alahayam, who made the heaven, the earth, the sea, and all that is in them;
who by the mouth of your servant, Dawad, said, ‘Why do the nations rage, and the peoples plot a vain thing?
The kings of the earth take a stand, and the rulers take council together, against the Adanay, and against his Mashayach.’
“For truly, both Hawaradawas and Pontius Payalatawas, with the Gentiles and the people of Yasharaal, were gathered together against your holy servant, Yashawai, whom you anointed,
to do whatever your hand and your council foreordained to happen.
Now, Adanay, look at their threats, and grant to your servants to speak your word with all boldness,
while you stretch out your hand to heal; and that signs and wonders may be done through the name of your holy Servant Yashawai.”
When they had prayed, the place was shaken where they were gathered together. They were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and they spoke the word of Alahayam with boldness.
The multitude of those who believed were of one heart and soul. Not one of them claimed that anything of the things which he possessed was his own, but they had all things in common.
With great power, the apostles gave their testimony of the resurrection of the Adanay Yashawai. Great grace was on them all.
For neither was there among them any who lacked, for as many as were owners of lands or houses sold them, and brought the proceeds of the things that were sold,
and laid them at the apostles’ feet, and distribution was made to each, according as anyone had need.
Joses, who by the apostles was also called Baranab (which is, being interpreted, Son of Encouragement), a Levite, a man of Cyprus by race,
having a field, sold it and brought the money and laid it at the apostles’ feet.
But a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira, his wife, sold a possession,
and kept back part of the price, his wife also being aware of it, then brought a certain part and laid it at the apostles’ feet.
But Kayapaa said, “Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit and to keep back part of the price of the land?
While you kept it, didn’t it remain your own? After it was sold, wasn’t it in your power? How is it that you have conceived this thing in your heart? You haven’t lied to men, but to Alahayam.”
Ananias, hearing these words, fell down and died. Great fear came on all who heard these things.
The young men arose and wrapped him up, and they carried him out and buried him.
About three hours later, his wife, not knowing what had happened, came in.
Kayapaa answered her, “Tell me whether you sold the land for so much.” She said, “Yes, for so much.”

But Kayapaa asked her, “How is it that you have agreed together to tempt the Spirit of the Adanay? Behold, the feet of those who have buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out.”
She fell down immediately at his feet and died. The young men came in and found her dead, and they carried her out and buried her by her husband.
Great fear came on the whole assembly, and on all who heard these things.
By the hands of the apostles many signs and wonders were done among the people. They were all with one accord in Shalamah’s porch.
None of the rest dared to join them, however the people honored them.
More believers were added to the Adanay, multitudes of both men and women.
They even carried out the sick into the streets, and laid them on cots and mattresses, so that as Kayapaa came by, at the least his shadow might overshadow some of them.
The multitude also came together from the cities around Yarawashalam, bringing sick people and those who were tormented by unclean spirits: and they were all healed.
But the high priest rose up, and all those who were with him (which is the sect of the Sadducees), and they were filled with jealousy
and laid hands on the apostles, then put them in public custody.
But an angel of the Adanay opened the prison doors by night, and brought them out and said,
“Go stand and speak in the temple to the people all the words of this life.”

When they heard this, they entered into the temple about daybreak and taught. But the high priest came, and those who were with him, and called the council together, and all the senate of the children of Yasharaal, and sent to the prison to have them brought.
But the officers who came didn’t find them in the prison. They returned and reported,
“We found the prison shut and locked, and the guards standing before the doors, but when we opened them, we found no one inside!”
Now when the high priest, the captain of the temple, and the chief priests heard these words, they were very perplexed about them and what might become of this.
One came and told them, “Behold, the men whom you put in prison are in the temple, standing and teaching the people.”
Then the captain went with the officers, and brought them without violence, for they were afraid that the people might stone them.
When they had brought them, they set them before the council. The high priest questioned them,
saying, “Didn’t we strictly command you not to teach in this name? Behold, you have filled Yarawashalam with your teaching, and intend to bring this man’s blood on us.”
But Kayapaa and the apostles answered, “We must obey Alahayam rather than men.
The Alahayam of our fathers raised up Yashawai, whom you killed, hanging him on a tree.
Alahayam exalted him with his right hand to be a Prince and a Savior, to give repentance to Yasharaal, and remission of sins.
We are his witnesses of these things; and so also is the Holy Spirit, whom Alahayam has given to those who obey him.”
But they, when they heard this, were cut to the heart, and were determined to kill them.
But one stood up in the council, a Pharisee named Gamalayaal, a teacher of the law, honored by all the people, and commanded to put the apostles out for a little while.
He said to them, “You men of Yasharaal, be careful concerning these men, what you are about to do.

For before these days Theudas rose up, making himself out to be somebody; to whom a number of men, about four hundred, joined themselves. He was slain; and all, as many as obeyed him, were dispersed, and came to nothing.
After this man, Yahawadah of Galayal rose up in the days of the enrollment, and drew away some people after him. He also perished, and all, as many as obeyed him, were scattered abroad.
Now I tell you, withdraw from these men, and leave them alone. For if this counsel or this work is of men, it will be overthrown.
But if it is of Alahayam, you will not be able to overthrow it, and you would be found even to be fighting against Alahayam!”
They agreed with him. Summoning the apostles, they beat them and commanded them not to speak in the name of Yashawai, and let them go.
They therefore departed from the presence of the council, rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer dishonor for Yashawai’ name.
Every day, in the temple and at home, they never stopped teaching and preaching Yashawai, the Mashayach.
Now in those days, when the number of the disciples was multiplying, a complaint arose from the Hellenists against the Hebrews, because their widows were neglected in the daily service.
The twelve summoned the multitude of the disciples and said, “It is not appropriate for us to forsake the word of Alahayam and serve tables.
Therefore select from among you, brothers, seven men of good report, full of the Holy Spirit and of wisdom, whom we may appoint over this business.
But we will continue steadfastly in prayer and in the ministry of the word.”
These words pleased the whole multitude. They chose Satapan, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, Payalayapawas, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolaus, a proselyte of Antioch;
whom they set before the apostles. When they had prayed, they laid their hands on them.
The word of Alahayam increased and the number of the disciples greatly multiplied in Yarawashalam. A great company of the priests were obedient to the faith.
Satapan, full of faith and power, performed great wonders and signs among the people.
But some of those who were of the synagogue called “The Libertines”, and of the Cyrenians, of the Alexandrians, and of those of Cilicia and Asia arose, disputing with Satapan.
They weren’t able to withstand the wisdom and the Spirit by which he spoke.
Then they secretly induced men to say, “We have heard him speak blasphemous words against Mashah and Alahayam.”
They stirred up the people, the elders, and the scribes, and came against him and seized him, then brought him in to the council,
and set up false witnesses who said, “This man never stops speaking blasphemous words against this holy place and the law.
For we have heard him say that this Yashawai of Natzarath will destroy this place, and will change the customs which Mashah delivered to us.”
All who sat in the council, fastening their eyes on him, saw his face like it was the face of an angel.
The high priest said, “Are these things so?”
He said, “Brothers and fathers, listen. The Alahayam of glory appeared to our father Abaraham when he was in Aram, before he lived in Charan,
and said to him, ‘Get out of your land and away from your relatives, and come into a land which I will show you.’
Then he came out of the land of the Chaldaeans and lived in Charan. From there, when his father was dead, Alahayam moved him into this land, where you are now living.
He gave him no inheritance in it, no, not so much as to set his foot on. He promised that he would give it to him for a possession, and to his offspring after him, when he still had no child.
Alahayam spoke in this way: that his offspring would live as aliens in a strange land, and that they would be enslaved and mistreated for four hundred years.
‘I will judge the nation to which they will be in bondage,’ said Alahayam, ‘and after that they will come out, and serve me in this place.’

He gave him the covenant of circumcision. So Abaraham became the father of Yatzachaq, and circumcised him the eighth day. Yatzachaq became the father of Yaiqab, and Yaiqab became the father of the twelve patriarchs.
“The patriarchs, moved with jealousy against Yawasap, sold him into Matzarayam. Alahayam was with him,
and delivered him out of all his afflictions, and gave him favor and wisdom before Paraih, king of Matzarayam. He made him governor over Matzarayam and all his house.
Now a famine came over all the land of Matzarayam and Kanain, and great affliction. Our fathers found no food.
But when Yaiqab heard that there was grain in Matzarayam, he sent out our fathers the first time.
On the second time Yawasap was made known to his brothers, and Yawasap’s race was revealed to Paraih.
Yawasap sent and summoned Yaiqab, his father, and all his relatives, seventy-five souls.
Yaiqab went down into Matzarayam and he died, himself and our fathers,
and they were brought back to Shakam, and laid in the tomb that Abaraham bought for a price in silver from the children of Chamawar of Shakam.
“But as the time of the promise came close which Alahayam had sworn to Abaraham, the people grew and multiplied in Matzarayam,
until there arose a different king, who didn’t know Yawasap.
The same took advantage of our race, and mistreated our fathers, and forced them to throw out their babies, so that they wouldn’t stay alive.
At that time Mashah was born, and was exceedingly handsome. He was nourished three months in his father’s house.
When he was thrown out, Paraih’s daughter took him up and reared him as her own son.
Mashah was instructed in all the wisdom of the Matzarayam. He was mighty in his words and works.
But when he was forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the children of Yasharaal.
Seeing one of them suffer wrong, he defended him, and avenged him who was oppressed, striking the Matzarayam.
He supposed that his brothers understood that Alahayam, by his hand, was giving them deliverance; but they didn’t understand.
“The day following, he appeared to them as they fought, and urged them to be at peace again, saying, ‘Sirs, you are brothers. Why do you wrong one another?’
But he who did his neighbor wrong pushed him away, saying, ‘Who made you a ruler and a judge over us?
Do you want to kill me, as you killed the Matzarayam yesterday?’
Mashah fled at this saying, and became a stranger in the land of Madayan, where he became the father of two sons.
“When forty years were fulfilled, an angel of the Adanay appeared to him in the wilderness of Mount Sayanay, in a flame of fire in a bush.
When Mashah saw it, he wondered at the sight. As he came close to see, a voice of the Adanay came to him,
‘I am the Alahayam of your fathers, the Alahayam of Abaraham, the Alahayam of Yatzachaq, and the Alahayam of Yaiqab.’ Mashah trembled, and dared not look.
The Adanay said to him, ‘Take off your sandals, for the place where you stand is holy ground.
I have surely seen the affliction of my people that is in Matzarayam, and have heard their groaning. I have come down to deliver them. Now come, I will send you into Matzarayam.’
“This Mashah, whom they refused, saying, ‘Who made you a ruler and a judge?’—Alahayam has sent him as both a ruler and a deliverer by the hand of the angel who appeared to him in the bush.
This man led them out, having worked wonders and signs in Matzarayam, in the Red Sea, and in the wilderness for forty years.
This is that Mashah, who said to the children of Yasharaal, ‘The Adanay our Alahayam will raise up a prophet for you from among your brothers, like me.’
This is he who was in the assembly in the wilderness with the angel that spoke to him on Mount Sayanay, and with our fathers, who received living revelations to give to us,
to whom our fathers wouldn’t be obedient, but rejected him, and turned back in their hearts to Matzarayam,
saying to Aharan, ‘Make us gods that will go before us, for as for this Mashah, who led us out of the land of Matzarayam, we don’t know what has become of him.’
They made a calf in those days, and brought a sacrifice to the idol, and rejoiced in the works of their hands.

But Alahayam turned, and gave them up to serve the army of the sky, as it is written in the book of the prophets, ‘Did you offer to me slain animals and sacrifices forty years in the wilderness, O house of Yasharaal?
You took up the tabernacle of Moloch, the star of your god Rephan, the figures which you made to worship. I will carry you away beyond Babal.’
“Our fathers had the tabernacle of the testimony in the wilderness, even as he who spoke to Mashah commanded him to make it according to the pattern that he had seen;
which also our fathers, in their turn, brought in with Yahawashai when they entered into the possession of the nations, whom Alahayam drove out before the face of our fathers, to the days of Dawad,
who found favor in the sight of Alahayam, and asked to find a habitation for the Alahayam of Yaiqab.
But Shalamah built him a house.
However, the Most High doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands, as the prophet says,
‘heaven is my throne, and the earth a footstool for my feet. What kind of house will you build me?’ says the Adanay. ‘Or what is the place of my rest?
Didn’t my hand make all these things?’
“You stiff-necked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, you always resist the Holy Spirit! As your fathers did, so you do.
Which of the prophets didn’t your fathers persecute? They killed those who foretold the coming of the Righteous One, of whom you have now become betrayers and murderers.
You received the law as it was ordained by angels, and didn’t keep it!”
Now when they heard these things, they were cut to the heart, and they gnashed at him with their teeth.
But he, being full of the Holy Spirit, looked up steadfastly into heaven and saw the glory of Alahayam, and Yashawai standing on the right hand of Alahayam,
and said, “Behold, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of Alahayam!”
But they cried out with a loud voice and stopped their ears, then rushed at him with one accord.
They threw him out of the city and stoned him. The witnesses placed their garments at the feet of a young man named Shaawal.
They stoned Satapan as he called out, saying, “Adanay Yashawai, receive my spirit!”
He kneeled down, and cried with a loud voice, “Adanay, don’t hold this sin against them!” When he had said this, he fell asleep.

Shaawal was consenting to his death. A great persecution arose against the assembly which was in Yarawashalam in that day. They were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Yahawadah and Shamarawan, except for the apostles.
Devout men buried Satapan and lamented greatly over him.
But Shaawal ravaged the assembly, entering into every house and dragged both men and women off to prison.
Therefore those who were scattered abroad went around preaching the word.
Payalayapawas went down to the city of Shamarawan, and proclaimed to them the Mashayach.
The multitudes listened with one accord to the things that were spoken by Payalayapawas when they heard and saw the signs which he did.
For unclean spirits came out of many of those who had them. They came out, crying with a loud voice. Many who had been paralyzed and lame were healed.
There was great joy in that city.
But there was a certain man, Shamaiwan by name, who used to practice sorcery in the city and amazed the people of Shamarawan, making himself out to be some great one,
to whom they all listened, from the least to the greatest, saying, “This man is that great power of Alahayam.”
They listened to him, because for a long time he had amazed them with his sorceries.
But when they believed Payalayapawas preaching good news concerning Alahayam’s Kingdom and the name of Yashawai Mashayach, they were baptized, both men and women.
Shamaiwan himself also believed. Being baptized, he continued with Payalayapawas. Seeing signs and great miracles occurring, he was amazed.
Now when the apostles who were at Yarawashalam heard that Shamarawan had received the word of Alahayam, they sent Kayapaa and Yawachanan to them,
who, when they had come down, prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Spirit;
for as yet he had fallen on none of them. They had only been baptized in the name of Mashayach Yashawai.
Then they laid their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.
Now when Shamaiwan saw that the Holy Spirit was given through the laying on of the apostles’ hands, he offered them money,
saying, “Give me also this power, that whomever I lay my hands on may receive the Holy Spirit.”
But Kayapaa said to him, “May your silver perish with you, because you thought you could obtain the gift of Alahayam with money!
You have neither part nor lot in this matter, for your heart isn’t right before Alahayam.
Repent therefore of this, your wickedness, and ask Alahayam if perhaps the thought of your heart may be forgiven you.
For I see that you are in the poison of bitterness and in the bondage of iniquity.”
Shamaiwan answered, “Pray for me to the Adanay, that none of the things which you have spoken happen to me.”
They therefore, when they had testified and spoken the word of the Adanay, returned to Yarawashalam, and preached the Good News to many villages of the Samaritans.
But an angel of the Adanay spoke to Payalayapawas, saying, “Arise, and go toward the south to the way that goes down from Yarawashalam to Izah. This is a desert.”
He arose and went; and behold, there was a man of Kawash, a eunuch of great authority under Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, who was over all her treasure, who had come to Yarawashalam to worship.
He was returning and sitting in his chariot, and was reading the prophet Yashaiyahaw.
The Spirit said to Payalayapawas, “Go near, and join yourself to this chariot.”
Payalayapawas ran to him, and heard him reading Yashaiyahaw the prophet, and said, “Do you understand what you are reading?”
He said, “How can I, unless someone explains it to me?” He begged Payalayapawas to come up and sit with him.
Now the passage of the Scripture which he was reading was this, “He was led as a sheep to the slaughter. As a lamb before his shearer is silent, so he doesn’t open his mouth.
In his humiliation, his judgment was taken away. Who will declare His generation? For his life is taken from the earth.”
The eunuch answered Payalayapawas, “Who is the prophet talking about? About himself, or about someone else?”
Payalayapawas opened his mouth, and beginning from this Scripture, preached to him about Yashawai.
As they went on the way, they came to some water, and the eunuch said, “Behold, here is water. What is keeping me from being baptized?”
He commanded the chariot to stand still, and they both went down into the water, both Payalayapawas and the eunuch, and he baptized him.
When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Adanay caught Payalayapawas away, and the eunuch didn’t see him any more, for he went on his way rejoicing.
But Payalayapawas was found at Azotus. Passing through, he preached the Good News to all the cities, until he came to Caesarea.
But Shaawal, still breathing threats and slaughter against the disciples of the Adanay, went to the high priest
and asked for letters from him to the synagogues of Damashaq, that if he found any who were of the Way, whether men or women, he might bring them bound to Yarawashalam.
As he traveled, he got close to Damashaq, and suddenly a light from the sky shone around him.
He fell on the earth, and heard a voice saying to him, “Shaawal, Shaawal, why do you persecute me?”
He said, “Who are you, Adanay?” The Adanay said, “I am Yashawai, whom you are persecuting.
But rise up and enter into the city, then you will be told what you must do.”
The men who traveled with him stood speechless, hearing the sound, but seeing no one.
Shaawal arose from the ground, and when his eyes were opened, he saw no one. They led him by the hand, and brought him into Damashaq.
He was without sight for three days, and neither ate nor drank.
Now there was a certain disciple at Damashaq named Ananias. The Adanay said to him in a vision, “Ananias!” He said, “Behold, it’s me, Adanay.”
The Adanay said to him, “Arise, and go to the street which is called Straight, and inquire in the house of Yahawadah for one named Shaawal, a man of Tarsus. For behold, he is praying,
and in a vision he has seen a man named Ananias coming in and laying his hands on him, that he might receive his sight.”
But Ananias answered, “Adanay, I have heard from many about this man, how much evil he did to your saints at Yarawashalam.
Here he has authority from the chief priests to bind all who call on your name.”
But the Adanay said to him, “Go your way, for he is my chosen vessel to bear my name before the nations and kings, and the children of Yasharaal.
For I will show him how many things he must suffer for my name’s sake.”

Ananias departed and entered into the house. Laying his hands on him, he said, “Brother Shaawal, the Adanay, who appeared to you on the road by which you came, has sent me that you may receive your sight and be filled with the Holy Spirit.”
Immediately something like scales fell from his eyes, and he received his sight. He arose and was baptized.
He took food and was strengthened. Shaawal stayed several days with the disciples who were at Damashaq.
Immediately in the synagogues he proclaimed the Mashayach, that he is the Son of Alahayam.
All who heard him were amazed, and said, “Isn’t this he who in Yarawashalam made havoc of those who called on this name? And he had come here intending to bring them bound before the chief priests!”
But Shaawal increased more in strength, and confounded the Jews who lived at Damashaq, proving that this is the Mashayach.
When many days were fulfilled, the Jews conspired together to kill him,
but their plot became known to Shaawal. They watched the gates both day and night that they might kill him,
but his disciples took him by night and let him down through the wall, lowering him in a basket.
When Shaawal had come to Yarawashalam, he tried to join himself to the disciples; but they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple.

But Baranab took him and brought him to the apostles, and declared to them how he had seen the Adanay on the way, and that he had spoken to him, and how at Damashaq he had preached boldly in the name of Yashawai.
He was with them entering into Yarawashalam,
preaching boldly in the name of the Adanay Yashawai. He spoke and disputed against the Hellenists, but they were seeking to kill him.
When the brothers knew it, they brought him down to Caesarea, and sent him off to Tarsus.
So the assemblies throughout all Yahawadah, Galayal, and Shamarawan had peace, and were built up. They were multiplied, walking in the fear of the Adanay and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit.
As Kayapaa went throughout all those parts, he came down also to the saints who lived at Lydda.
There he found a certain man named Aeneas, who had been bedridden for eight years, because he was paralyzed.
Kayapaa said to him, “Aeneas, Yashawai Mashayach heals you. Get up and make your bed!” Immediately he arose.
All who lived at Lydda and in Sharawan saw him, and they turned to the Adanay.
Now there was at Yapaw a certain disciple named Tabitha, which when translated, means Dorcas. This woman was full of good works and acts of mercy which she did.
In those days, she became sick, and died. When they had washed her, they laid her in an upper room.
As Lydda was near Yapaw, the disciples, hearing that Kayapaa was there, sent two men to him, imploring him not to delay in coming to them.

Kayapaa got up and went with them. When he had come, they brought him into the upper room. All the widows stood by him weeping, and showing the coats and garments which Dorcas had made while she was with them.
Kayapaa sent them all out, and knelt down and prayed. Turning to the body, he said, “Tabitha, get up!” She opened her eyes, and when she saw Kayapaa, she sat up.
He gave her his hand, and raised her up. Calling the saints and widows, he presented her alive.
This became known throughout all Yapaw, and many believed in the Adanay.
He stayed many days in Yapaw with a tanner named Shamaiwan.
Now there was a certain man in Caesarea, Cornelius by name, a centurion of what was called the Italian Regiment,
a devout man, and one who feared Alahayam with all his house, who gave gifts for the needy generously to the people, and always prayed to Alahayam.
At about the ninth hour of the day, he clearly saw in a vision an angel of Alahayam coming to him, and saying to him, “Cornelius!”
He, fastening his eyes on him, and being frightened, said, “What is it, Adanay?” He said to him, “Your prayers and your gifts to the needy have gone up for a memorial before Alahayam.
Now send men to Yapaw, and get Shamaiwan, who is also called Kayapaa.
He is staying with a tanner named Shamaiwan, whose house is by the seaside.
When the angel who spoke to him had departed, Cornelius called two of his household servants and a devout soldier of those who waited on him continually.
Having explained everything to them, he sent them to Yapaw.
Now on the next day as they were on their journey, and got close to the city, Kayapaa went up on the housetop to pray at about noon.
He became hungry and desired to eat, but while they were preparing, he fell into a trance.
He saw heaven opened and a certain container descending to him, like a great sheet let down by four corners on the earth,
in which were all kinds of four-footed animals of the earth, wild animals, reptiles, and birds of the sky.
A voice came to him, “Rise, Kayapaa, kill and eat!”
But Kayapaa said, “Not so, Adanay; for I have never eaten anything that is common or unclean.”
A voice came to him again the second time, “What Alahayam has cleansed, you must not call unclean.”
This was done three times, and immediately the vessel was received up into heaven.

Now while Kayapaa was very perplexed in himself what the vision which he had seen might mean, behold, the men who were sent by Cornelius, having made inquiry for Shamaiwan’s house, stood before the gate,
and called and asked whether Shamaiwan, who was also called Kayapaa, was lodging there.
While Kayapaa was pondering the vision, the Spirit said to him, “Behold, three men seek you.
But arise, get down, and go with them, doubting nothing; for I have sent them.”
Kayapaa went down to the men, and said, “Behold, I am he whom you seek. Why have you come?”

They said, “Cornelius, a centurion, a righteous man and one who fears Alahayam, and well spoken of by all the nation of the Jews, was directed by a holy angel to invite you to his house, and to listen to what you say.”
So he called them in and provided a place to stay. On the next day Kayapaa arose and went out with them, and some of the brothers from Yapaw accompanied him.
On the next day they entered into Caesarea. Cornelius was waiting for them, having called together his relatives and his near friends.
When Kayapaa entered, Cornelius met him, fell down at his feet, and worshiped him.
But Kayapaa raised him up, saying, “Stand up! I myself am also a man.”
As he talked with him, he went in and found many gathered together.

He said to them, “You yourselves know how it is an unlawful thing for a man who is a Yahawaday to join himself or come to one of another nation, but Alahayam has shown me that I shouldn’t call any man unholy or unclean.
Therefore I also came without complaint when I was sent for. I ask therefore, why did you send for me?”
Cornelius said, “Four days ago, I was fasting until this hour, and at the ninth hour, I prayed in my house, and behold, a man stood before me in bright clothing,
and said, ‘Cornelius, your prayer is heard, and your gifts to the needy are remembered in the sight of Alahayam.
Send therefore to Yapaw, and summon Shamaiwan, who is also called Kayapaa. He is staying in the house of a tanner named Shamaiwan, by the seaside. When he comes, he will speak to you.’
Therefore I sent to you at once, and it was good of you to come. Now therefore we are all here present in the sight of Alahayam to hear all things that have been commanded you by Alahayam.”
Kayapaa opened his mouth and said, “Truly I perceive that Alahayam doesn’t show favoritism;
but in every nation he who fears him and works righteousness is acceptable to him.
The word which he sent to the children of Yasharaal, preaching good news of peace by Yashawai Mashayach—he is Adanay of all—
you yourselves know what happened, which was proclaimed throughout all Yahawadah, beginning from Galayal, after the baptism which Yawachanan preached;
even Yashawai of Natzarath, how Alahayam anointed him with the Holy Spirit and with power, who went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, for Alahayam was with him.
We are witnesses of everything he did both in the country of the Jews, and in Yarawashalam; whom they also killed, hanging him on a tree.
Alahayam raised him up the third day, and gave him to be revealed,
not to all the people, but to witnesses who were chosen before by Alahayam, to us, who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead.
He commanded us to preach to the people and to testify that this is he who is appointed by Alahayam as the Judge of the living and the dead.
All the prophets testify about him, that through his name everyone who believes in him will receive remission of sins.”
While Kayapaa was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell on all those who heard the word.
They of the circumcision who believed were amazed, as many as came with Kayapaa, because the gift of the Holy Spirit was also poured out on the Gentiles.
For they heard them speaking in other languages and magnifying Alahayam. Then Kayapaa answered,
“Can anyone forbid these people from being baptized with water? They have received the Holy Spirit just like us.”
He commanded them to be baptized in the name of Yashawai Mashayach. Then they asked him to stay some days.
Now the apostles and the brothers who were in Yahawadah heard that the Gentiles had also received the word of Alahayam.
When Kayapaa had come up to Yarawashalam, those who were of the circumcision contended with him,
saying, “You went in to uncircumcised men, and ate with them!”
But Kayapaa began, and explained to them in order, saying,
“I was in the city of Yapaw praying, and in a trance I saw a vision: a certain container descending, like it was a great sheet let down from heaven by four corners. It came as far as me.
When I had looked intently at it, I considered, and saw the four-footed animals of the earth, wild animals, creeping things, and birds of the sky.
I also heard a voice saying to me, ‘Rise, Kayapaa, kill and eat!’
But I said, ‘Not so, Adanay, for nothing unholy or unclean has ever entered into my mouth.’
But a voice answered me the second time out of heaven, ‘What Alahayam has cleansed, don’t you call unclean.’
This was done three times, and all were drawn up again into heaven.
Behold, immediately three men stood before the house where I was, having been sent from Caesarea to me.
The Spirit told me to go with them, without discriminating. These six brothers also accompanied me, and we entered into the man’s house.
He told us how he had seen the angel standing in his house, and saying to him, ‘Send to Yapaw, and get Shamaiwan, who is called Kayapaa,
who will speak to you words by which you will be saved, you and all your house.’
As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell on them, even as on us at the beginning.
I remembered the word of the Adanay, how he said, ‘Yawachanan indeed baptized in water, but you will be baptized in the Holy Spirit.’
If then Alahayam gave to them the same gift as us, when we believed in the Adanay Yashawai Mashayach, who was I, that I could withstand Alahayam?”
When they heard these things, they held their peace, and glorified Alahayam, saying, “Then Alahayam has also granted to the Gentiles repentance to life!”
They therefore who were scattered abroad by the oppression that arose about Satapan traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, speaking the word to no one except to Jews only.
But there were some of them, men of Cyprus and Cyrene, who, when they had come to Antioch, spoke to the Hellenists, preaching the Adanay Yashawai.
The hand of the Adanay was with them, and a great number believed and turned to the Adanay.
The report concerning them came to the ears of the assembly which was in Yarawashalam. They sent out Baranab to go as far as Antioch,
who, when he had come, and had seen the grace of Alahayam, was glad. He exhorted them all, that with purpose of heart they should remain near to the Adanay.
For he was a good man, and full of the Holy Spirit and of faith, and many people were added to the Adanay.
Baranab went out to Tarsus to look for Shaawal.
When he had found him, he brought him to Antioch. For a whole year they were gathered together with the assembly, and taught many people. The disciples were first called Christians in Antioch.
Now in these days, prophets came down from Yarawashalam to Antioch.
One of them named Agabus stood up, and indicated by the Spirit that there should be a great famine all over the world, which also happened in the days of Claudius.
As any of the disciples had plenty, each determined to send relief to the brothers who lived in Yahawadah;
which they also did, sending it to the elders by the hands of Baranab and Shaawal.
Now about that time, King Hawaradawas stretched out his hands to oppress some of the assembly.
He killed Yaiqab, the brother of Yawachanan, with the sword.
When he saw that it pleased the Jews, he proceeded to seize Kayapaa also. This was during the days of unleavened bread.
When he had arrested him, he put him in prison, and delivered him to four squads of four soldiers each to guard him, intending to bring him out to the people after the Passover.
Kayapaa therefore was kept in the prison, but constant prayer was made by the assembly to Alahayam for him.
The same night when Hawaradawas was about to bring him out, Kayapaa was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains. Guards in front of the door kept the prison.
And behold, an angel of the Adanay stood by him, and a light shone in the cell. He struck Kayapaa on the side, and woke him up, saying, “Stand up quickly!” His chains fell off his hands.
The angel said to him, “Get dressed and put on your sandals.” He did so. He said to him, “Put on your cloak and follow me.”
And he went out and followed him. He didn’t know that what was being done by the angel was real, but thought he saw a vision.

When they were past the first and the second guard, they came to the iron gate that leads into the city, which opened to them by itself. They went out, and went down one street, and immediately the angel departed from him.

When Kayapaa had come to himself, he said, “Now I truly know that the Adanay has sent out his angel and delivered me out of the hand of Hawaradawas, and from everything the Jewish people were expecting.”
Thinking about that, he came to the house of Marayam, the mother of Yawachanan who was called Mark, where many were gathered together and were praying.
When Kayapaa knocked at the door of the gate, a servant girl named Rhoda came to answer.
When she recognized Kayapaa’s voice, she didn’t open the gate for joy, but ran in, and reported that Kayapaa was standing in front of the gate.
They said to her, “You are crazy!” But she insisted that it was so. They said, “It is his angel.”
But Kayapaa continued knocking. When they had opened, they saw him, and were amazed.

But he, beckoning to them with his hand to be silent, declared to them how the Adanay had brought him out of the prison. He said, “Tell these things to Yaiqab and to the brothers.” Then he departed and went to another place.
Now as soon as it was day, there was no small stir among the soldiers about what had become of Kayapaa.
When Hawaradawas had sought for him, and didn’t find him, he examined the guards, then commanded that they should be put to death. He went down from Yahawadah to Caesarea, and stayed there.

Now Hawaradawas was very angry with the people of Tzar and Tzayadawan. They came with one accord to him, and, having made Blastus, the king’s personal aide, their friend, they asked for peace, because their country depended on the king’s country for food.
On an appointed day, Hawaradawas dressed himself in royal clothing, sat on the throne, and gave a speech to them.
The people shouted, “The voice of a god, and not of a man!”
Immediately an angel of the Adanay struck him, because he didn’t give Alahayam the glory. Then he was eaten by worms and died.
But the word of Alahayam grew and multiplied.
Baranab and Shaawal returned to Yarawashalam when they had fulfilled their service, also taking with them Yawachanan who was called Mark.

Now in the assembly that was at Antioch there were some prophets and teachers: Baranab, Shamaiwan who was called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen the foster brother of Hawaradawas the tetrarch, and Shaawal.
As they served the Adanay and fasted, the Holy Spirit said, “Separate Baranab and Shaawal for me, for the work to which I have called them.”
Then, when they had fasted and prayed and laid their hands on them, they sent them away.
So, being sent out by the Holy Spirit, they went down to Seleucia. From there they sailed to Cyprus.
When they were at Salamis, they proclaimed Alahayam’s word in the Jewish synagogues. They also had Yawachanan as their attendant.
When they had gone through the island to Paphos, they found a certain sorcerer, a false prophet, a Yahawaday, whose name was Bar Yashawai,
who was with the proconsul, Sergius Paulus, a man of understanding. This man summoned Baranab and Shaawal, and sought to hear the word of Alahayam.
But Elymas the sorcerer (for so is his name by interpretation) withstood them, seeking to turn the proconsul away from the faith.
But Shaawal, who is also called Shaawal, filled with the Holy Spirit, fastened his eyes on him,
and said, “You son of the devil, full of all deceit and all cunning, you enemy of all righteousness, will you not cease to pervert the right ways of the Adanay?

Now, behold, the hand of the Adanay is on you, and you will be blind, not seeing the sun for a season!” Immediately a mist and darkness fell on him. He went around seeking someone to lead him by the hand.
Then the proconsul, when he saw what was done, believed, being astonished at the teaching of the Adanay.
Now Shaawal and his company set sail from Paphos, and came to Perga in Pamphylia. Yawachanan departed from them and returned to Yarawashalam.
But they, passing on from Perga, came to Antioch of Pisidia. They went into the synagogue on the Sabbath day, and sat down.
After the reading of the law and the prophets, the rulers of the synagogue sent to them, saying, “Brothers, if you have any word of exhortation for the people, speak.”
Shaawal stood up, and beckoning with his hand said, “Men of Yasharaal, and you who fear Alahayam, listen.
The Alahayam of this people chose our fathers, and exalted the people when they stayed as aliens in the land of Matzarayam, and with an uplifted arm, he led them out of it.
For a period of about forty years he put up with them in the wilderness.
When he had destroyed seven nations in the land of Kanain, he gave them their land for an inheritance for about four hundred fifty years.
After these things, he gave them judges until Shamawaal the prophet.
Afterward they asked for a king, and Alahayam gave to them Shaawal the son of Qayash, a man of the tribe of Banayaman, for forty years.
When he had removed him, he raised up Dawad to be their king, to whom he also testified, ‘I have found Dawad the son of Yashay, a man after my heart, who will do all my will.’
From this man’s offspring, Alahayam has brought salvation to Yasharaal according to his promise,
before his coming, when Yawachanan had first preached the baptism of repentance to Yasharaal.
As Yawachanan was fulfilling his course, he said, ‘What do you suppose that I am? I am not he. But behold, one comes after me, the sandals of whose feet I am not worthy to untie.’
Brothers, children of the stock of Abaraham, and those among you who fear Alahayam, the word of this salvation is sent out to you.
For those who dwell in Yarawashalam, and their rulers, because they didn’t know him, nor the voices of the prophets which are read every Sabbath, fulfilled them by condemning him.
Though they found no cause for death, they still asked Payalatawas to have him killed.
When they had fulfilled all things that were written about him, they took him down from the tree, and laid him in a tomb.
But Alahayam raised him from the dead,
and he was seen for many days by those who came up with him from Galayal to Yarawashalam, who are his witnesses to the people.
We bring you good news of the promise made to the fathers,
that Alahayam has fulfilled this to us, their children, in that he raised up Yashawai. As it is also written in the second psalm, ‘You are my Son. Today I have become your father.’
“Concerning that he raised him up from the dead, now no more to return to corruption, he has spoken thus: ‘I will give you the holy and sure blessings of Dawad.’
Therefore he says also in another psalm, ‘You will not allow your Holy One to see decay.’
For Dawad, after he had in his own generation served the counsel of Alahayam, fell asleep, was laid with his fathers, and saw decay.
But he whom Alahayam raised up saw no decay.
Be it known to you therefore, brothers, that through this man is proclaimed to you remission of sins,
and by him everyone who believes is justified from all things, from which you could not be justified by the law of Mashah.
Beware therefore, lest that come on you which is spoken in the prophets:
‘Behold, you scoffers, and wonder, and perish; for I work a work in your days, a work which you will in no way believe, if one declares it to you.’ ”
So when the Jews went out of the synagogue, the Gentiles begged that these words might be preached to them the next Sabbath.
Now when the synagogue broke up, many of the Jews and of the devout proselytes followed Shaawal and Baranab; who, speaking to them, urged them to continue in the grace of Alahayam.
The next Sabbath, almost the whole city was gathered together to hear the word of Alahayam.
But when the Jews saw the multitudes, they were filled with jealousy, and contradicted the things which were spoken by Shaawal, and blasphemed.

Shaawal and Baranab spoke out boldly, and said, “It was necessary that Alahayam’s word should be spoken to you first. Since indeed you thrust it from yourselves, and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, behold, we turn to the Gentiles.
For so has the Adanay commanded us, saying, ‘I have set you as a light for the Gentiles, that you should bring salvation to the uttermost parts of the earth.’ ”
As the Gentiles heard this, they were glad, and glorified the word of Alahayam. As many as were appointed to eternal life believed.
The Adanay’s word was spread abroad throughout all the region.
But the Jews stirred up the devout and prominent women and the chief men of the city, and stirred up a persecution against Shaawal and Baranab, and threw them out of their borders.
But they shook off the dust of their feet against them, and came to Iconium.
The disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.
In Iconium, they entered together into the synagogue of the Jews, and so spoke that a great multitude both of Jews and of Greeks believed.
But the disbelieving Jews stirred up and embittered the souls of the Gentiles against the brothers.
Therefore they stayed there a long time, speaking boldly in the Adanay, who testified to the word of his grace, granting signs and wonders to be done by their hands.
But the multitude of the city was divided. Part sided with the Jews, and part with the apostles.
When some of both the Gentiles and the Jews, with their rulers, made a violent attempt to mistreat and stone them,
they became aware of it and fled to the cities of Lycaonia, Lystra, Derbe, and the surrounding region.
There they preached the Good News.
At Lystra a certain man sat, impotent in his feet, a cripple from his mother’s womb, who never had walked.
He was listening to Shaawal speaking, who, fastening eyes on him, and seeing that he had faith to be made whole,
said with a loud voice, “Stand upright on your feet!” He leaped up and walked.
When the multitude saw what Shaawal had done, they lifted up their voice, saying in the language of Lycaonia, “The gods have come down to us in the likeness of men!”
They called Baranab “Jupiter”, and Shaawal “Mercury”, because he was the chief speaker.
The priest of Jupiter, whose temple was in front of their city, brought oxen and garlands to the gates, and would have made a sacrifice along with the multitudes.
But when the apostles, Baranab and Shaawal, heard of it, they tore their clothes, and sprang into the multitude, crying out,

“Men, why are you doing these things? We also are men of like passions with you, and bring you good news, that you should turn from these vain things to the living Alahayam, who made the sky, the earth, the sea, and all that is in them;
who in the generations gone by allowed all the nations to walk in their own ways.
Yet he didn’t leave himself without witness, in that he did good and gave you rains from the sky and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness.”
Even saying these things, they hardly stopped the multitudes from making a sacrifice to them.
But some Jews from Antioch and Iconium came there, and having persuaded the multitudes, they stoned Shaawal, and dragged him out of the city, supposing that he was dead.
But as the disciples stood around him, he rose up, and entered into the city. On the next day he went out with Baranab to Derbe.
When they had preached the Good News to that city, and had made many disciples, they returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch,
strengthening the souls of the disciples, exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that through many afflictions we must enter into Alahayam’s Kingdom.
When they had appointed elders for them in every assembly, and had prayed with fasting, they commended them to the Adanay, on whom they had believed.
They passed through Pisidia, and came to Pamphylia.
When they had spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.
From there they sailed to Antioch, from where they had been committed to the grace of Alahayam for the work which they had fulfilled.
When they had arrived, and had gathered the assembly together, they reported all the things that Alahayam had done with them, and that he had opened a door of faith to the nations.
They stayed there with the disciples for a long time.
Some men came down from Yahawadah and taught the brothers, “Unless you are circumcised after the custom of Mashah, you can’t be saved.”

Therefore when Shaawal and Baranab had no small discord and discussion with them, they appointed Shaawal and Baranab, and some others of them, to go up to Yarawashalam to the apostles and elders about this question.
They, being sent on their way by the assembly, passed through both Phoenicia and Shamarawan, declaring the conversion of the Gentiles. They caused great joy to all the brothers.
When they had come to Yarawashalam, they were received by the assembly and the apostles and the elders, and they reported everything that Alahayam had done with them.
But some of the sect of the Pharisees who believed rose up, saying, “It is necessary to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Mashah.”
The apostles and the elders were gathered together to see about this matter.

When there had been much discussion, Kayapaa rose up and said to them, “Brothers, you know that a good while ago Alahayam made a choice among you that by my mouth the nations should hear the word of the Good News and believe.
Alahayam, who knows the heart, testified about them, giving them the Holy Spirit, just like he did to us.
He made no distinction between us and them, cleansing their hearts by faith.
Now therefore why do you tempt Alahayam, that you should put a yoke on the neck of the disciples which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?
But we believe that we are saved through the grace of the Adanay Yashawai, just as they are.”
All the multitude kept silence, and they listened to Baranab and Shaawal reporting what signs and wonders Alahayam had done among the nations through them.
After they were silent, Yaiqab answered, “Brothers, listen to me.
